pass_a_gloss: What need is there for my silence, which has happened many times to many others, but to me especially now, being forced to be silent both willingly and unwillingly. For I have neglected and I am neglecting the good and beautiful words, which are spoken or composed by the chosen and approved names and verbs in a certain uninterrupted sequence. I, who am less capable of this pleasant Greek work. But now eight years have passed for me, during which I have not myself said or written anything great or small, nor have I heard from another who has written or said something, except for the wonderful men who have established beautiful philosophy, to whom elegance and simplicity of names are of less concern. They, placing their voices second, wish to examine and proclaim the matters themselves with precision. I do not think they do not want to, but rather they very much want to, and they pour out the good and precise thoughts with ease and clarity in speech. But perhaps they are not able to do so, having the sacred and divine word in their minds, and the pleasant word in their expressions, two things that are difficult for each person to possess, and to encompass the human soul, which is complex and human. If indeed silence is somehow a friend and helper to the mind and discovery. The one who is eloquent, you will not find anywhere else, except in voices and the continuous practice of them. But the mind also learns something else, and the mouth is bound by the tongue, if I wanted to say something, even small, to the Greek voice, our wonderful leaders, to whom now the affairs of all humans under the same authority are directed, not being hindered or learning effortlessly, being themselves accurate and varied and wonderful, and being called completely Greek, having been expressed and handed down to the Roman voice, which is persuasive and boastful and adapted to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. But in no other way is it possible or desirable for me. Since, however, our words are nothing but images of the passions of our soul, to those who are able to speak, like good painters and skilled craftsmen, who write with colors that are not only similar but also varied and beautiful, with a mixture of flowers, we would agree that they write without any hindrance.
pass_b_english: What need is there for my silence, which has happened many times to many others, but to me especially now, as I am being forced to be silent both willingly and unwillingly? For I have neglected, and I am still neglecting, the good and beautiful words that are spoken or composed by the chosen and approved names and verbs in a certain uninterrupted sequence. I, who am less capable of this pleasant Greek work, have now gone eight years without saying or writing anything great or small, nor have I heard from another who has written or said something, except for the wonderful men who have established beautiful philosophy, to whom elegance and simplicity of names are of less concern. They place their voices second and wish to examine and proclaim the matters themselves with precision, pouring out the good and precise thoughts with ease and clarity in speech. Perhaps, though, they are not able to do so, having the sacred and divine word in their minds, and the pleasant word in their expressions - two things that are difficult for each person to possess, and to encompass the human soul, which is complex and human. If indeed silence is somehow a friend and helper to the mind and discovery, then the one who is eloquent will not find this ability anywhere else, except in voices and the continuous practice of them. But the mind also learns something else, and the mouth is bound by the tongue, so if I wanted to say something, even small, to the Greek voice, I would be speaking to our wonderful leaders, to whom the affairs of all humans under the same authority are now directed, and who are not hindered or learning effortlessly, being themselves accurate and varied and wonderful, and being called completely Greek, having been expressed and handed down to the Roman voice, which is persuasive and boastful and adapted to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. Since, however, our words are nothing but images of the passions of our soul, to those who are able to speak, like good painters and skilled craftsmen, who write with colors that are not only similar but also varied and beautiful, with a mixture of flowers, we would agree that they write without any hindrance, and this is the state of things now.
